source.basemap_imagery: GEBCO web map service (wms.gebco.net), layer GEBCO_LATEST
source.provenance: GEBCO Type Identifier (TID) grid, queried per point via WMS GetFeatureInfo

tid_codes.10-17: direct measurement (11 = multibeam sonar, 17 = combined direct)
tid_codes.40: predicted from satellite-derived gravity (interpolated, not sounded)

point_provenance.feature: Puerto Rico Trench deepest grid cell

puerto_rico_trench_axis.note: Trench floor is fully multibeam-surveyed; the -8555 m cell is measured, not an interpolation artifact (this corrects an earlier assumption).

cayman_trough_axis.note: The deepest reported reach is satellite-predicted, not sounded; predicted bathymetry under-reads narrow trenches, so the true floor is probably deeper than the grid shows.

texture_experiment.question: Can satellite-predicted seafloor be detected from depth texture alone (no TID)?

coarse_metric_5km_detrended_rms.verdict: weak; apparent 75% classifier accuracy was a base-rate artifact (73% of samples predicted)

cellscale_metric_laplacian_rms.verdict: works; predicted seafloor is 3.6x smoother at the cell scale (below satellite gravity's ~6 km resolution), enabling ~76% blind classification

coverage_vs_depth.note: Non-monotonic; coverage follows survey effort, not depth. Overall ~73% of sampled Cayman seafloor is predicted, not sounded.
